title: SEBI's Performance-Linked Fee vs. TER: What It Means for Your Mutual Funds
description: SEBI has proposed a new framework to link mutual fund fees directly to a scheme's performance. This model aims to replace or supplement the existing Total Exp.

faq.q: What is the Total Expense Ratio (TER)?
faq.a: The TER is the annual cost of operating a mutual fund, expressed as a percentage of its assets. It covers management fees, administrative costs, and other expenses, deducted from the fund's NAV daily.

faq.q: How is a performance-linked fee different from TER?
faq.a: A performance-linked fee is variable and directly tied to how well a fund performs against a pre-defined benchmark. Unlike a fixed TER, it can increase with outperformance and decrease with underperformance.

faq.q: Will the new model replace TER entirely?
faq.a: The exact implementation is still being discussed by SEBI. It could potentially replace the TER, or it might be an additional component to a base TER.

faq.q: What is a 'hurdle rate' in this context?
faq.a: A hurdle rate is a minimum return a mutual fund must achieve before it is eligible to charge a performance-based fee. If the fund's returns are below this rate, no performance fee is charged.

The high-water mark ensures that a fund manager only earns a performance fee if the fund's Net Asset Value (NAV) surpasses its previous highest NAV. This prevents managers from earning fees for simply recovering past losses.

faq.q: When is this new fee model expected to be implemented?
faq.a: The proposal is currently under discussion with industry stakeholders. There is no definitive timeline for its implementation yet, and it will likely undergo further refinements based on feedback.

faq.q: How will this impact my existing mutual fund investments?
faq.a: If implemented, the new fee structure would likely apply to all mutual fund schemes, including your existing investments, as per SEBI's regulations. However, specific transition rules would be announced.
